title: India–New Zealand Trade Deal: Why Zero Duty Isn’t Both Ways
description: The India–New Zealand free trade agreement took effect on 20 October 2026. This current-affairs explainer compares tariff treatment by direction and explains why rules of origin and other costs still matter.
hook: New Zealand dropped duties on qualifying Indian exports. Did India do the same?
payoff: Remember the test: which direction are the goods going, and do they qualify?

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: New Zealand dropped duties on qualifying Indian exports. Did India do the same?

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: No. The free trade agreement took effect on October twentieth, twenty twenty-six, with different terms each way.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: Qualifying Indian goods enter New Zealand without customs duty, the tax charged on imports.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: The New Zealand government said almost fifty-seven percent of its exports to India were tariff-free at launch.
units.onscreen: NEW ZEALAND → INDIA: ALMOST 57% AT LAUNCH

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: That's export coverage, not a count of tariff lines. India kept exclusions, including dairy.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: Rules of origin decide which goods qualify. Shipping from a partner country isn't enough.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: And zero customs duty does not erase other charges or product requirements.
